questions.questionTextEn: The atmosphere is a mixture of several gases. Near the earth surface it contains mainly:
questions.questionTextHi: [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1997] The atmosphere is a mixture of several gases. Near the earth surface it contains mainly:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A) Nitrogen and oxygen. The atmosphere is a mixture of different gases, of which 99% are mainly Nitrogen (78.084%) and Oxygen(20.947%). Remaining approximately 1% are Argon, Carbon dioxide, Neon, Helium, Methane, Hydrogen, Nitrous Oxide, Ozone, Krypton, Xenon, etc. Heavy gases are found at the bottom of atmosphere and light gases are found at the top. [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1997]

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following is the permanent gas in the atmosphere?
questions.questionTextHi: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2017] Which one of the following is the permanent gas in the atmosphere?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Nitrogen. Permanent gases in the atmosphere are those gases which quantity does not change from day to day. These gas pri- marily contain nitrogen, oxygen and argon. Except these three gases, the quantity of CO 2 Ozone and Neon keep on changing according to the circumstances. [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2017]

questions.questionTextEn: The correct sequence of different layers of the atmosphere from the surface of the Earth upwards is :
questions.questionTextHi: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1998] The correct sequence of different layers of the atmosphere from the surface of the Earth upwards is :
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Ionosphere. On the basis of temperature and air pressure atmosphere is divided into five layers starting from the earth’s surface which are as follows : Troposphere- (15 km from the surface of the earth) Stratosphere (15-50 km) Mesosphere (50-80 km) Ionosphere (80-640 km) Exosphere (above more than 640 km) The thermo sphere is located above the mesosphere and below the exosphere, and its lowest part contains Inosphere. [I.A.S. (Pre) 1998]

questions.questionTextHi: [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1999] Most weather activity occurs in which atmospheric layer:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Troposphere. Almost all the weather phenomena like rainfall, fog and hailstorm, etc. occur in the troposphere. The temperature in this layer decreases at the rate of 6.5°C for every 1000 meter (1 km) height. [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1999]

questions.questionTextEn: The stratosphere is said to be ideal for flying jet aircraft. This is because-
questions.questionTextHi: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] The stratosphere is said to be ideal for flying jet aircraft. This is because-
optionsEn: This layer is rich in ozone which reduces fuel consumption
The temperature is constant and ideal for aircraft engine efficiency
This layer is out of the firing range of antiaircraft guns
The absence of clouds and other weather phenomena
optionsHi: This layer is rich in ozone which reduces fuel consumption
The temperature is constant and ideal for aircraft engine efficiency
This layer is out of the firing range of antiaircraft guns
The absence of clouds and other weather phenomena
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D) The absence of clouds and other weather phenomena. The stratosphere is the second major layer of Earth’s atmosphere, just above the troposphere, and below the mesosphere. The stratosphere is very dry and air of this layer contains little water vapour. Because of this, Stratosphere is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomenon. [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010]

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Stratosphere. The ozone layer is mainly found in the lower portion of the stratosphere from 15 to 35 kilometres above Earth. This layer absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the Earth from an intense and harmful form of energy. [State PSC / UPSC PYQ]

questions.questionTextEn: Which layer of atmosphere is responsible for Aurora Borealis?
questions.questionTextHi: [U.P.P.C.S (Pre) 2010] Which layer of atmosphere is responsible for Aurora Borealis?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Ionosphere. Aurora is an incredible light caused by collisions between electrically charged particles released from the Sun that enter the Earth atmosphere. Aurora that occurs in the Northern Hemisphere is called 'Aurora Borealis' and in Southern Hemisphere is called 'Aurora Australis'. The light of Aurora extends from (80 Km to 640 Km). [U.P.P.C.S (Pre) 2010]
